chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn Al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people! I do not want to find a man who has a deceased person and waits with him until morning, nor a man who has a deceased person during the day and waits with him until night. Do not wait with your dead for the sunrise or the sunset. Hasten them to their resting places. May Allah have mercy on you.'
So the people said, 'And you, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you.'

key_terms.يَرْحَمُكُمُ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on you

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on delaying burial?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) instructs the community to hasten the burial of the deceased, avoiding unnecessary delays such as waiting for sunrise or sunset. This teaching emphasizes efficiency and respect in handling the dead, promising divine mercy for those who comply. The Prophet's own affirmation, 'And you, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you,' highlights the communal acceptance of this practice as a model of piety and promptness in fulfilling religious duties.
